data.hypothesis: The measured 8x64 full-height tile was faster than baseline (3.061 μs versus 3.494 μs), while the 8x16 subtile was slower (3.839 μs); those timings do not establish a cause. Widening the full-height pencil to 16 may improve x coalescing and reduce the grid from 512 to 256 blocks versus 8x64, but doubles the block to 1024 threads and may reduce occupancy. This isolates the wider full-slab tradeoff while retaining the existing halo logic for correctness.

memory_lessons.applicability: Motivates measuring a contrasting 16x64 full-height tile; timings alone do not identify the cause of the 8x16 regression.
memory_lessons.claim: The valid 8x64 candidate measured 3.06111993268 μs mean, compared with 3.49397328682 μs for baseline. The valid 8x16 candidate measured 3.838613396513333e-06 seconds. These outcomes show different measured latencies, not their causes.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure a 16x64 full-height shared-memory tile with the controller’s correctness oracle and full-run event latency.

data.notes: This is a single pencil-width experiment: the active y-derivative block becomes 16x64, while coefficients, shared-memory halo mapping, barriers, buffers, entry point, and launch path remain unchanged. No new correctness or latency measurement is available; leave those to the controller.
transformations: Set sPencils to 16, producing a 16-wide x pencil while retaining the full 64-row y slab in the active derivative_y block.
Keep the existing radius-4 shared-memory halo assignments, including the period-63 endpoint mapping, and both barriers.
Preserve the stencil coefficients, arithmetic expression, output mapping, buffers, entry point, and launch model.
